body.html: Kampu Resort is a small, family-run place with only about 12 rooms, set inside Na Ban village on the front side of the island. It's worth being clear up front: this is not a beachfront or pier-side property — the resort's own site notes the accommodation is not by the sea. What it is, is a spot in the village that's a roughly 6-minute walk from Na Ban Pier and under 1 km from Tawaen Beach. Its appeal isn't the view; it's the value and the convenience packed into a budget price.

What sets Kampu apart from similarly priced stays is what's bundled into the rate. Breakfast is included, there's a free transfer from the pier (you call when your boat lands, rather than paying for a songthaew into the village), and there's a free motorbike to ride out to the island's beaches. On Koh Larn, those three together meaningfully cut your per-trip cost — transport and bike rental are the line items most people forget to budget for.
"Clean room, kind owner who picked us up at the pier, a free motorbike to explore on, and breakfast too — at this price it's genuinely great value for Koh Larn."

Rooms are simple — clean and functional, with air-con, a fridge, hot water and Wi-Fi. Real guest reviews line up on cleanliness and the owner's friendliness; many mention helpful tips on where to go and eat and easy help with logistics. The average sits around 9.0 on Agoda from a few dozen reviews, with roughly 4.5 of 5 on TripAdvisor — though the review count is still smaller than the island's bigger operators.

Things to know before booking: there's no pool, no sea view, and you're in a village you'll need to walk or ride out from to reach a beach. This is a guesthouse-style small resort, not a fully-equipped beach resort. The Na Ban village location has its upsides (walk to shops, restaurants, the market and the pier) and its limits (busy with day-trippers by day, quiet at night, beaches need the motorbike). Anyone expecting a beachfront-resort feel may find it doesn't match the picture.

Honestly, Kampu Resort suits travellers doing Koh Larn on a budget — out on the beaches all day, back to sleep at night. If your picture is someone meeting you at the pier, a free bike to explore on, breakfast before you head out, and a clean room at a low price — it delivers, and it's good value. But if you want a pool, a sea-view room, or to step straight from your door onto sand, a place over on Tawaen or Samae Beach will fit better.

On price, standard rooms start around ฿1,600/night (off-peak it has dipped toward ฿1,500 and climbs toward ฿1,800–2,000 on holidays). With only about 12 rooms and several extras bundled in, weekends and long holidays fill fast. Listed online prices aren't always current, so compare a few platforms and message the resort's Line/Facebook page to check availability and any current deals before you commit.

faq.q: Where on Koh Larn is Kampu Resort, and is it on the beach?
faq.a: It's in Na Ban village on Koh Larn, Bang Lamung, Chon Buri. It is not on the beach or directly on the pier, but it's a ~6-minute walk from Na Ban Pier and under 1 km from Tawaen Beach. You can walk to shops, restaurants and the market in the village; for the beaches, use the free motorbike the resort provides.

faq.q: How much does Kampu Resort cost, and what's included?
faq.a: From approx. ฿1,600/night for a standard room (off-peak it has dipped toward ฿1,500, climbing toward ฿1,800–2,000 on holidays). The rate includes breakfast, a free pier transfer and a free motorbike to ride. Online prices aren't always current — compare a few platforms and message the resort's page before booking.

faq.q: Does Kampu Resort have a swimming pool?
faq.a: No pool. It's a small resort of about 12 rooms in the village, built around value and extras (breakfast, free pier transfer, free motorbike) rather than big-resort facilities. If you need a pool, look at a resort or pool villa on the beach side instead.

faq.q: How do I get from the pier to Kampu Resort?
faq.a: Take the ferry from Bali Hai Pier in Pattaya to Na Ban Pier on Koh Larn (about 45 minutes). When you land, call the resort for the free pickup — no need to pay for a songthaew into the village — or simply walk the ~6 minutes.

faq.q: Who is Kampu Resort best for?
faq.a: Best for budget travellers out on the beaches all day, back to sleep at night. You get the full bundle (breakfast, free pier transfer, free motorbike) at a low price. Less ideal if you want a sea view, a pool, or to step straight from your room onto the sand.

faq.q: Does Kampu Resort have breakfast and Wi-Fi?
faq.a: Yes to both. The room rate includes breakfast and there's free Wi-Fi. Rooms have air-con, a fridge and hot water. Per resort policy, children aged 0–4 stay free (one per room, sharing the parents' bed).
